question: Your CI pipeline runs Claude Code with the -p flag to review each pull request. An independent verification pass then reports one confidence score for the whole review, and thresholds calibrated on a labeled validation set decide whether the review is posted directly or held for the maintainers. Auto-posted reviews still contain some false-positive comments, and held reviews make the maintainers check many findings that are clearly correct. What is the most likely cause of this routing problem?

options.text: The routing thresholds were set by checking the verification scores against a labeled validation set instead of being chosen by the maintainers from their own review experience.
options.reason: The guide recommends calibrating confidence thresholds with labeled validation sets. Calibration is the correct method, so it is not the cause of this routing problem.

options.text: The verification pass gives one confidence score per review instead of a confidence level for each finding, so routing cannot separate doubtful findings from sure ones.
options.reason: The guide has the verification pass report confidence alongside each finding to enable calibrated review routing. A single score per review sends sure and doubtful findings down the same path.

options.text: The review covers every changed file in one pass instead of per-file passes plus an integration pass, which causes attention dilution and contradictory findings across the review.
options.reason: The guide uses per-file and integration passes to improve detection in large reviews. That does not explain why routing posts doubtful findings and holds sure ones inside the same review.

options.text: The pipeline runs Claude Code with the -p flag in non-interactive mode, so the verification pass cannot ask the maintainers questions before it scores a review.
options.reason: The guide names the -p flag as the way to run Claude Code in CI. Non-interactive mode does not cause the mix of sure and doubtful findings in one routing decision.
